architecture.approach: One feature-flagged module, crates/wirekit/src/meta.rs, behind a default-off meta feature, following the existing provider modules. Transport, retry, rate limiting, tracing, and Secret handling are reused unchanged; the feature adds no new dependency and no runtime.

dataModel.flowDescription: The caller builds MetaClient from caller-supplied credentials, picks a surface, builds SendMessageRequest, and the module posts through WirekitClient. Failures flatten the nested Graph error into WirekitError::Api. Inbound, the caller passes raw bytes plus X-Hub-Signature-256; the module verifies, parses, and returns MetaEvent.

securityConsiderations.description: Tokens and the app secret are held in Secret and render as *** in Debug; no environment reads (CON-511, CON-519).
The page or phone-number identity comes from configuration, not the message body, so a caller cannot address another page (CON-512).
Inbound bodies are size-bounded and parsed into typed events; unknown types become an explicit unsupported variant (CON-515).
Base URLs are validated as HTTPS at client construction (CON-520).

risks.description: Meta app review and page-token permissions are unconfirmed, so live calls may fail with permission errors.
risks.mitigation: Verify against a local mock, as m5-gated-integrations did, and keep the assumption marked [to be confirmed].

risks.description: Graph API version churn changes paths and payloads.
risks.mitigation: Single API_VERSION constant, asserted per surface.

risks.description: Instagram and Messenger differ in host and token scope despite a shared payload shape.
risks.mitigation: One request type, two hosts, asserted per surface.
